newsitem.title: USA: Saudi minister cites "progress" in bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Saudi minister cites "progress" in bomb probe.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's defence minister said on Wednesday that Saudi investigators were making progress in the investigation of a truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen, but that the probe would not be rushed.

"We have not finished the investigation. We are not pointing fingers yet at anybody," Prince Sultan told reporters during a visit to the Pentagon when asked about the June 25 bombing near Dhahran. "We are trying to make sure justice is seen to be done and therefore we don't want to rush the investigation unnecessarily. But there is progress."

Sultan did not elaborate on the progress. His comments came as he was greeted by Defense Secretary William Cohen for talks midway through a five-day Washington visit by senior Saudi ministers to reaffirm close ties marred by U.S. concerns over the probe into the truck bombing.

Washington has complained that Saudi Arabia is not sharing enough information with the FBI on its investigation of the Dhahran blast, which followed another Saudi car bombing in Riyadh in late 1995 that killed five Americans.
"Our cooperation with our friends is going in an excellent way and as soon as all the investigation is complete we plan to reveal all the details," Sultan told reporters.

Sultan met President Bill Clinton on Tuesday and will hold talks with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Thursday, He and a delegation that includes the Saudi foreign, oil and trade ministers will stay until Friday.
